item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Which shape has a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A right triangle with the 90 degree angle in the bottom left.]

item.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A half-turn about point P in the plane is applied to the shaded figure.

[Image: Shaded figure on dashed axes]

Which of the following shows the results of the half-turn?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with rightmost vertex at point P]

reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem diagram, a horizontal dashed line and a vertical dashed line intersect perpendicularly at point P, which is marked with a black dot and labeled P below the horizontal line. A shaded right triangle lies above the horizontal dashed line. Its bottom horizontal base lies along the horizontal dashed line, extending both to the left and to the right of point P, with the segment to the left of P being longer than the segment to the right of P. The right edge of the triangle is vertical, extending upward from the horizontal line. The hypotenuse connects the top-right vertex to the leftmost vertex on the horizontal dashed line. The vertical dashed line passes through the shaded triangle.

Option A shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the right.
Option B shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the left of P), its vertical side on the right extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the left.
Option C shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line, vertical side on the right extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the left.
Option D shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the right.
Option E shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line located entirely to the left of point P, touching point P at its rightmost acute vertex, with its vertical side on the left extending downward.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?

options.label: A
options.text: I and II

options.label: B
options.text: I and III

options.label: C
options.text: I and IV

options.label: D
options.text: II and IV

options.label: E
options.text: III and IV

reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The line m is a line of symmetry for figure ABCDE.

The measure of angle BCD is

[Image: Polygon ABCDE with line of symmetry m]
reference_items.figure_description: A symmetric five-sided polygon ABCDE with a vertical dashed line of symmetry labeled m, which has arrows at both top and bottom ends. The horizontal top side connects vertex A on the left to vertex E on the right, bisected perpendicularly by line m. The left side goes down and outward from A to vertex B, then slants down and inward to vertex C at the bottom, which lies on line m. The right side is a mirror image, going from E down and outward to vertex D, then down and inward to vertex C. Inside the polygon, angle A is marked with an arc and labeled 130, angle B is marked with an arc and labeled 110, and the angle between side BC and line of symmetry m at vertex C is marked with an arc and labeled 30.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Triangular prism]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles connected in a V-shape by two triangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles and two triangles on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles and three triangles]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles, one triangle on the top right and one triangle on the bottom left]

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three right-angled triangles labeled Figure 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3 from left to right:
- Figure 1: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical left side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute right-most vertex.
- Figure 2: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-right corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical right side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute left-most vertex.
- Figure 3: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a shorter horizontal base, and a longer vertical left side. A horizontal line segment connects the vertical left side to the hypotenuse near the acute top vertex.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. The right most angle of the triangle adjacent to the larger triangle has an angle of 30 degrees. The smaller triangle contained within the bigger triangle has an angle x that is formed by the right side of the triangle and the drawn line.]

In the figure above, what is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two parallel lines, M and N. M lies above N. Two lines are drawn over M and N. One goes up from the left to the right, and the other one goes down, from the left to the right. The two lines intersect N at two different points, but meet at a common point on line M. This forms a triangle between lines M and N. The top angle of this triangle is angle B. The right most angle of this triangle is 70 degrees. The line that goes up from the left to the right intersects line M at a 60 degree angle.]

Lines m and n are parallel.

What is the value of b?

Answer: ____

descriptors: Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shows 2/3 of the square shaded?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Square divided horizontally into six equal strips with the top two strips shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle at the bottom and shaded regions above]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three strips with the two narrow outer strips shaded]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle spanning from the bottom edge to the top center and two shaded triangles on the sides]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three equal strips with the two outer strips shaded]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
